what: Manual review of the 5 sampled answers that the regex in run_experiments.py flagged as naming George Eliot (runs/sample.json). This is a judgment, not a computation.
reviewed_by: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), 2026-09-27; to be spot-checked by Aditya Raj
rule: Counts as 'names George Eliot as the author' only if the answer attributes Middlemarch to her.

runs.excerpt: The first part of the book was written by George Eliot, a Nobel Laureate in Literature.
invented_facts: 'a Nobel Laureate in Literature' — the Nobel Prize in Literature was first awarded in 1901; Eliot died in 1880
'originally titled "The Mill at Frome"' — no such title; The Mill on the Floss is a different Eliot novel

runs.excerpt: The names of many authors associated with the work of George Eliot, including her most famous novel, The Melivalm by Charles Barsanti…
runs.note: Mentions Eliot but attributes a (non-existent) novel to someone else; does not say she wrote Middlemarch.

runs.excerpt: The author of the book Middlemarch is George Eliot… Eliot's work was first published in 1870…
The author behind Middlemarch is George Eliot… Her novel won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1885…
invented_facts: 'Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1885' — the Pulitzer Prizes were first awarded in 1917, and the fiction prize is for American authors

sources.eliot_dates_and_publication: Project Gutenberg eBook #145, Middlemarch: 'Eliot, George, 1819-1880'; 'a novel published in 1871-1872' — https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/145
sources.nobel: Wikipedia, Nobel Prize in Literature: 'In 1901, French poet and essayist Sully Prudhomme … was the first person to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature' — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Literature
sources.pulitzer: Wikipedia, Pulitzer Prize: 'First awarded in June 1917'; fiction prize 'for distinguished fiction by an American author' — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize
